issue.title: provider: TestOpenCodeProjectIs225s and TestOpenCodeEnvironmentIs225s red when a .git sits above the temp folder
issue.body:
Both are red on a Linux box whose /tmp has an empty `.git` folder in it (not mine, owned by nobody), run alone at origin/main 43849d51:

```
--- FAIL: TestOpenCodeProjectIs225s (0.00s)
    opencode_v2_test.go:178: /tmp/TestOpenCodeProjectIs225s487823157/001/plain: 470c8549ef01a2a9d3c85b22965766cefc874134, want sha1("directory:/tmp/TestOpenCodeProjectIs225s487823157/001/plain")
    opencode_v2_test.go:186: no folder: 470c8549ef01a2a9d3c85b22965766cefc874134, want the home folder's
--- FAIL: TestOpenCodeEnvironmentIs225s (0.00s)
    opencode_v2_test.go:211: block ... Workspace root folder: /tmp ...
```

openCodeRepository walks up from the folder to the nearest `.git` and takes one with no config as a repository without a remote, so the plain fixture folder and the test's home both come out as the repository at /tmp. The same happens anywhere the temp folder sits under a `.git`, a TMPDIR inside a checkout for one. I haven't checked whether OpenCode 2.2.5 itself takes an empty `.git` as a repository: if it doesn't, magpie's walk is off for that case; if it does, the tests need a folder with no `.git` above it, which t.TempDir() can't promise. Not taking it.

comments.body:
A test-only fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5239-opencode-fixture-git-boundary), commit [a4f6d0af5](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/a4f6d0af59d229fc73506981a5a3453073796fde), based on ed0ab567.

The plain-folder fixtures now have an empty `.git` file at their boundary. The existing detector treats a non-gitdir file as non-repository, so it stops before inheriting a checkout above TMPDIR; the nested real repository and worktree fixtures still take precedence. No test is skipped and production detection is unchanged.

The original project test fails with TMPDIR inside this checkout, inheriting its remote for the plain directory. Both original tests now pass with race with TMPDIR inside and outside the checkout, retaining the plain/home/repository/worktree/environment assertions. Provider vet, the full offline nogui build, formatting and diff checks pass. Native Windows/macOS and the full suite were not run. AI-assisted implementation and review.

The patch on #5995 fixes these two at the cause for the empty /tmp/.git case: OpenCode's project walk now passes over a .git that git doesn't take (as OpenCode 2.2.5 itself does, since it asks git rev-parse), and both tests pass in a full suite with it here. skygunner's fixture change above still covers the other case, a TMPDIR inside a real checkout, which my patch doesn't.

issue.body:

So the gui tests' requests through http.DefaultTransport go out to the network. At origin/main 532d054b a full `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -v ./internal/gui` here logs:

```
codex: Get "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models?client_version=0.159.0": read tcp ...: read: connection reset by peer
```

That one is TestAccountSaveKeepsPriceRate: it signs in a fixture ChatGPT account, and the account's Codex models are asked for behind the save. With `testenv.Offline()` added to the gui's TestMain, the same run refuses and logs these (the test named is the one running when the address was first asked):

- api.deepseek.com:443 (TestProviderSaveDecideEndpoint)
- api-inference.modelscope.cn:443 (TestProviderSaveKeepsCountFree)
- ws-9.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com:443 (TestProviderSystemOne)
- opencode.ai:443 (TestZenAddAnotherKeyEmptyAddsPublic)

- pics.example, films.example, example.invalid (TestImageModelsHidden, TestVideoModelsHidden, TestKeysImportAndRest)

Every gui test still passes with it but one, TestSteadyGCRetunesAfterACollection, which goes red for a reason of its own (#5256). I didn't check whether any of these tests' assertions count on the request going out. Patch in a comment below.

issue.title: gui: TestGatewayHeldByAContainer moves the port past a local magpie (setPort returns nil) in a full run on mote

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Red in a full `go test -timeout 45m ./...` run at 5957223d8 (v0.1.2901) on mote. Other sessions' e2e and GUI runs were on mote at the same time. Test took 29.12s:

```
--- FAIL: TestGatewayHeldByAContainer (29.12s)
    gateway_container_test.go:92: moved past a magpie of this computer's: <nil>
```

This is not #2107's or #3649's timeout. The fake "magpie" child answered `gateway.ServedBy()` as 0.1.550, but `setPort(freePort(t))` then returned nil and moved the port. The check that a magpie of this computer's holds the port said no, though the child was still running. The 29s spent before it suggests the owner lookup (proc.ListeningOn or similar) gave up or timed out under load and was read as "nobody", not as "unknown" (code standards: a failed read means unknown).

Not looked into further. The change in 5957223d8 touches only internal/library and docs.

issue.title: library, memory: a .git folder that isn't a repository (an empty one above the project) is taken for the project's repository

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
A `.git` folder that isn't a repository is taken for one when magpie looks up a folder's repository. The box I test on has an empty `/tmp/.git` (git says "not a git repository" anywhere under /tmp), so every test whose temp folder is under /tmp and that asks "which repository is this in" gets /tmp, and these are red at origin/main db0f2f20d:

```
--- FAIL: TestProjectOutsideGit (internal/library; also TestCodexProjectStartupTimeout, TestUpdateSkillRefreshesProjects)
    projects_test.go:171: problems: [{... What:project: Error:keeping it out of git: mkdir /tmp/.git/info: permission denied ...}]
--- FAIL: TestProjectOfIsTheRepository (internal/memory)
    project_test.go:67: a plain folder: &{Key:dir:/tmp Name:tmp Roots:[/tmp]}
--- FAIL: TestWhatIsSent (internal/memdistill)
    memdistill_test.go:200: not sent: "Project: proj"  (it got "Project: tmp")
```

The library ones are new with 87b3af765 (a project turns a server or skill off "out of git"), which writes into what it took for the repository's .git/info. The same lookup is in internal/library/project_git.go and internal/memory/project.go; #5239 (OpenCode's project id) is the same family in internal/provider.

A user with a stray empty .git above a project would see the same: the project counted as /tmp's (or their home's), and magpie trying to write an exclude file in it. I'm on a fix that asks what git asks (a .git folder with HEAD, or a .git file with a gitdir line) at the magpie-owned sites, leaving the ones that mirror another app's own rule alone unless that app does the same.

issue.title: proc: TestCombinedOutputOwnContext gets signal: killed, not context.Canceled

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
`TestCombinedOutputOwnContext` (internal/proc, disclaim_test.go:103) got the kill instead of the context's error:

```
--- FAIL: TestCombinedOutputOwnContext (0.04s)
    disclaim_test.go:103: err signal: killed, want canceled
```

When the context ends, the child is killed and its Wait can return `signal: killed` before the code checks `ctx.Err()`. Either CombinedOutput should report `ctx.Err()` whenever the context ended, or the test's want is too narrow. Which one a caller relies on decides it.

Seen in a full `go test -count=1 -timeout 45m -tags nogui ./...` at 6b92824ff (v0.1.3567) on the Linux box (WSL2 magpie-desktop), under ~/suite.lock but beside another session's unlocked `go test ./internal/claudetui/ ./internal/gateway/` on the same box, so the box was loaded. Log: magpie-wt/norethsea-scratch/suite.log. Not rerun alone; not reproduced with an injected delay.

issue.title: TestCappedIsSmall red: one HeapAlloc delta measured capped at 12,056 vs bounded 82,624 (6.9x, wants 10x)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
`TestCappedIsSmall` (internal/capre) failed in a full `go test -count=1 -timeout 45m ./...` run on the Linux box (wsl-run, magpie-desktop) at 2fbead798 (v0.1.3570):

```
--- FAIL: TestCappedIsSmall (0.05s)
    capre_test.go:59: held to a length: 12056 bytes, bounded 82624
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/capre	0.064s
```

The test measures `runtime.MemStats.HeapAlloc` before and after one `MustCompile` and wants the capped program to be under a tenth of the bounded one. Here capped measured 12,056 bytes (6.9x smaller, not 10x). A HeapAlloc delta counts whatever else the runtime allocated between the two reads (other goroutines, the testing framework, GC timing), so the capped side, being small, is the one noise moves. Suggest measuring something the program owns (e.g. `testing.AllocsPerRun`/`testing.Benchmark` bytes per op over many compiles, or the compiled program's instruction count) instead of one heap delta.

Not taken by me (found after the CRS fix's tag; the change doesn't touch capre).

issue.title: Plugins can't run on OpenWrt: libc.Musl() misses musl's own loader name, so magpie downloads Bun's glibc build

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

On OpenWrt (musl, aarch64) every plugin install fails. magpie picks Bun's **glibc** build and the host never starts:

```
fork/exec /root/.cache/magpie/bun/1.4.2/magpie-bun: no such file or directory
```

The file is there — 79 MB of it. What is missing is the interpreter it names.

## Why

`internal/libc/libc.go` decides musl by two hard-coded paths:

```go
var muslLoaders = []string{"/lib/libc.musl-x86_64.so.1", "/lib/libc.musl-aarch64.so.1"}
```

OpenWrt's musl does not use those names. It ships:

```
/lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1 -> libc.so
/lib/libc.so
```

Neither `libc.musl-aarch64.so.1` nor `libc.musl-x86_64.so.1` exists. So `libc.Musl()` returns `false`, `bunTarget()` takes the glibc branch, and the download needs `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`, which OpenWrt doesn't have. `execve` reports `ENOENT` for a missing interpreter exactly as it does for a missing file, hence the misleading message.

Confirmed on the device: after the plugin install fails, `~/.cache/magpie/bun/1.4.2/` exists but `~/.cache/magpie/bun/musl/` does not — magpie believes this is glibc.

This is a different root cause from #1877. That one was "there is no musl branch at all"; it is fixed. This is the **detection** still answering glibc on a musl system, because the two names it looks for are Alpine's packaging convention, not musl's own.

## Environment

- OpenWrt 25.12.5 r33051-f5dae5ece4, `armsr/armv8`, `aarch64_generic`
- Linux 6.18.54 aarch64, 8 cores, 1.5 GB RAM
- musl 1.2.x, `/lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1 -> libc.so`
- magpie v0.1.3395 (CLI build, no GUI: `magpie web --lan`)
- installed by hand into `/opt/magpie`, so `PackagedBy()` finds no package manager and the binary is not "stuck"

## Reproduce

```sh
apk add unzip   # OpenWrt has no unzip by default
curl -L -o magpie https://github.com/yetone/magpie/releases/download/v0.1.3395/magpie-cli-linux-arm64
chmod +x magpie && mv magpie /opt/magpie/magpie
MAGPIE_ADDR=0.0.0.0:3425 /opt/magpie/magpie web --lan --no-open
```

Then install any provider plugin from the Plugins page. All four I tried — `@magpie-community/opencode-trae-auth`, `opencode-loomy-auth`, `opencode-raccoon-auth`, `opencode-workbuddy-auth` — fail with the exec error above.

## Workaround that works here

**1. Give musl one of the names `libc.Musl()` looks for** — an idempotent symlink is enough:

```sh
ln -sf ld-musl-aarch64.so.1 /lib/libc.musl-aarch64.so.1
```

After this, `~/.cache/magpie/bun/musl/` appears and magpie picks `bun-linux-aarch64-musl.zip` by itself. This is the interesting half: the only thing wrong was the file name it stats.

**2. `MAGPIE_BUN` pointing at a good musl Bun**, so an update can never hand us a glibc build:

```sh
apk add libstdcpp6   # NOT libstdc++ — that is OpenWrt's package name for it
curl -L -o /tmp/bun.zip https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.4.2/bun-linux-aarch64-musl.zip
unzip -j /tmp/bun.zip '*/bun' -d /opt/magpie/bin && chmod +x /opt/magpie/bin/bun
export MAGPIE_BUN=/opt/magpie/bin/bun
```

Note `apk add libstdc++` fails with "no such package"; the OpenWrt name is `libstdcpp6`. Without it the musl Bun dies with `Error loading shared library libstdc++.so.6`.

## What a fix needs

`libc.Musl()` should also accept musl's own loader, which is the file that exists on every musl system and is not distro-renamed:

```go
var muslLoaders = []string{
	"/lib/libc.musl-x86_64.so.1",   // Alpine's name
	"/lib/libc.musl-aarch64.so.1",
	"/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1",     // musl's own loader, OpenWrt's name
	"/lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1",
}
```

Checking `/lib/ld-musl-<arch>.so.1` is strictly better than the `libc.musl-*` names: the loader is musl's own filename and every musl distribution has it under it, while `libc.musl-*` is Alpine's packaging convention. It also matches what #1877's fix already keys the cache directory off (`bunTarget()` returning a `-musl` target), so the two would agree.

Two follow-ups worth considering while in there:

- A downloaded Bun that fails `execve` with `ENOENT` now says "the build doesn't match this system's C library" (#1877 fixed that for the host's start). But **the plugin-install path still reports the bare exec error**, and nothing points at `MAGPIE_BUN`. Surfacing the same explanation there would have saved me an hour — the message I got reads like a missing file.
- `missingLibs()` suggests `apk add libstdc++ libgcc`. On OpenWrt the package is `libstdcpp6`, and there is no `libgcc` package at all (it ships in the base). Distro-specific advice can't be right everywhere, but `libstdcpp6` is worth naming for OpenWrt.

Happy to test a build on this device (OpenWrt 25.12.5, aarch64, real hardware) if that helps.

issue.title: update: a malformed 206 (Content-Range: bytes NaN-NaN/N) fails the resume hard, and the github.com fallback is never reached

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### magpie version
0.1.3602（手动装到 0.1.3605 后同样可复现）

### Where
GUI

### OS
Windows 11 (amd64)

### Agent, provider and model
无关，纯更新链路

### Steps to reproduce
1. 让 `magpie.exe.new` 的下载中途断掉（国内到 usemagpie.ai / GitHub 只有 ~33KB/s，89MB 基本必断）
2. magpie 的重试带着 `Range: bytes=<已下载字节>-` 去续传
3. 第一次硬失败：`update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content`，然后清掉已下载部分重来，永远循环

### What happened, and what you expected
更新永远失败。根因是官方文件端点对**任何** Range 请求都返回非法的 `Content-Range`：

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -H "Range: bytes=1000-1999" \
    https://usemagpie.ai/files/v0.1.3605/magpie-windows-amd64.exe
HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
Content-Length: 1000
Content-Range: bytes NaN-NaN/89400832      # ← 非法，RFC 7233 要求具体区间
```

不带 Range 时是正常的：

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -D - https://usemagpie.ai/files/v0.1.3605/magpie-windows-amd64.exe
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 89400832
```

而 feed 里的 `asset.github` 地址是好的：

```
$ curl -sL -o /dev/null -D - -H "Range: bytes=0-99" \
    https://github.com/yetone/magpie-releases/releases/download/v0.1.3605/magpie-windows-amd64.exe
HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
Content-Range: bytes 0-99/89400832         # ← 正常
```

于是 `internal/update/update.go` 里这条链必然走死：

- `fetch` 的 switch（约 1388 行）只接受 `206 && have > 0 && Content-Range` 以 `bytes <have>-` 开头；`NaN-NaN` 落到 `default`（约 1397–1401 行）→ `fmt.Errorf("download %s: %s", name, res.Status)`，正是日志里那句
- 这个 error 不是 `NetError`，所以 `download()`（约 1184 行）`if err == nil || ... || !Network(err) { break }` 直接跳出重试循环
- 也因此**永远不会走 1167 行起的 `a.GitHub` 回退**（它以 `busyErr(err) || try >= …` 为前提），明明 github.com 的 Range 是正常的

顺带：同一端点 4 次请求里有 2 次直接连不上（curl 返回 000），本身也不稳。

期望：断点续传遇到坏掉的 `Content-Range` 时不要硬失败。

### 建议的修法（任一）
1. 206 且 `have > 0` 时，`Content-Range` 解析不出区间但 `Content-Length == a.Size - have`，就当合法续传直接 append —— 用户即可自愈；
2. 或把这种非法 206 归到 `busyStatus` 那类「可重试/可换路」的错误，让 1167 行的 `a.GitHub` 回退接手；
3. 服务端 `usemagpie.ai/files/*` 的 Range 实现要修（`NaN-NaN` 应该是 `start-end/size`）。

### Error text or logs
```
2026/11/09 23:00:08 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 09:23:10 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:29:55 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:30:05 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:30:13 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:30:35 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:32:31 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:32:42 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:33:43 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:43:41 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 21:44:45 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
2026/11/10 22:15:14 update: download magpie.exe.new: 206 Partial Content
```
（11-08 的同一问题表现是 `504 Gateway Timeout`，路径同样不回落。）

绕过办法（已验证）：`curl -C -` 从 `github.com/yetone/magpie-releases/...` 拉全量，sha256 与 feed 对比一致后手动替换 exe。

issue.title: quota: a switched-off plan provider is printed as "balance · not configured · no balance endpoint known"

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Environment

- magpie **0.1.3358**, Windows 11, app mode
- provider **`opencode-go`**, one plan key whose windows magpie reads fine while the provider is on

## Steps

1. `magpie quota opencode-go --json` → `kind: "plan"`, windows `5 hours` / `7 days` / `Month` with `used` / `remaining` / `resetsAt`.
2. `magpie provider off opencode-go` → `✓ OpenCode Go is switched off: agents are given none of its models`
3. `magpie quota opencode-go --json` →

```json
[{"provider":"opencode-go","name":"OpenCode Go","kind":"balance","windows":[],
  "error":"not configured · no balance endpoint known for it; set Balance URL and Balance field in its editor"}]
```

Plain too: `opencode-go  balance  not configured · no balance endpoint known for it; set Balance URL and Balance field in its editor`

4. `magpie provider on opencode-go` → the plan windows are back, unchanged.

Reproduced consistently (read → off → read → on, twice).

## Why it is wrong

- Nothing is "not configured": the provider has a key and a plan whose windows are read every time it is on.
- The kind changes from `plan` to `balance` because the provider is no longer in the quota list — a switched-off provider is deliberately left alone (`docs/subsystems/providers-accounts.md`, `leftAlone`; #2226 settled that a switched-off account's allowance is not read in the background). `withUntold` in `internal/cli/quota_cli.go` then invents this row for any provider named that it did not find. The wording and `kind` were written for a provider that genuinely has no balance endpoint, not for one switched off.
- It sends the reader to edit a Balance URL that does not apply, and a script watching `magpie quota --json` cannot tell "switched off" from "misconfigured" — which matters when a provider is held out of rotation on purpose and its allowance still needs watching.

## Expected

Say what is true: the provider is switched off and magpie leaves it alone, so its windows are not read while it is off (optionally the last reading with its `readAt`, marked switched off). A fabricated `balance` / "not configured" row is not that.

## Related

- #2226 (closed) — a Codex subscription switched off or removed still had its allowance read and a reset spent (the rule that a switched-off provider is left alone)
- #4649 — when a vendor has no readable quota endpoint, let a provider declare its quota windows (the case that message was written for)

timeline.body: The patch on #5995 fixes these two at the cause for the empty /tmp/.git case: OpenCode's project walk now passes over a .git that git doesn't take (as OpenCode 2.2.5 itself does, since it asks git rev-parse), and both tests pass in a full suite with it here. skygunner's fixture change above still covers the other case, a TMPDIR inside a real checkout, which my patch doesn't.

issue.title: TestNoEagerPackageRegexps red on main: plugin.go and login_export.go compile a package-level regexp (fix on a fork branch)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
TestNoEagerPackageRegexps (root package) is red on main since 6af54dc9a, and again since b9f8548d2, each adding a package-level `regexp.MustCompile`:

```
--- FAIL: TestNoEagerPackageRegexps
    lazyre_test.go:72: internal/library/plugin.go:160:18: a package-level regexp is compiled at launch; use lazyre.New
    lazyre_test.go:72: internal/provider/login_export.go:158:20: a package-level regexp is compiled at launch; use lazyre.New
```

Red at 5d6935b1 and still at d2a80b31 on Linux. Fix: both go through `lazyre.New` like the rest since e4197144a, patterns and callers unchanged: [fix/plugin-name-lazyre](https://github.com/yinwu01/magpie/tree/fix/plugin-name-lazyre) (33868e08 on 5d6935b1, applies on d2a80b31 too, where the guard passes with it). library and provider pass whole except the reds this box has on main too (#5995, #5239); not tried on a Mac or Windows, nor the full suite. `git format-patch --no-signature --full-index --stdout 5d6935b1..33868e08 | sha256sum` is 00aaa633a14e882e7ab8a63a9a0f8420dde003ee26aa9dbd80317650c09b94b8.

issue.title: StdoutPipe read while another goroutine calls Wait: last output can be lost (siblings of #3741)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
1cb3dc435 (#3741) found that pf-serve's stdout came from cmd.StdoutPipe while a goroutine called cmd.Wait, which closes the pipe's read end once the process exits. A read after that gets "read |0: file already closed" instead of EOF. The error text reached the user, and output written just before the exit could be dropped. os/exec says it is incorrect to call Wait before all reads from the pipe have completed.

Places with the same shape still need checking, and fixing where Wait can run before the reader is done:
- internal/library/mcp_run.go:433: tree.Wait() in one goroutine, a Scanner over out in another (an MCP server's last JSON-RPC reply could be lost)
- internal/library/mcp_check.go:622
- internal/provider/claude_signin.go:186
- internal/provider/grok.go:581
- internal/claudetui/wslread.go:76

The fix pattern from 1cb3dc435: the caller makes its own os.Pipe, passes the write end as cmd.Stdout and closes it after Start, then closes the read end when the reader is done. Not changed in 1cb3dc435 itself, which only fixes pf-serve.

issue.title: gui: TestGatewayFixQuitsOnlyAMagpie names another process listening on the same port number (an emulator's qemu on mote)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Seen in the full suite (`go test -tags nogui -count=1 -timeout 45m ./...`, under mote's suite.lock) at 608c1543e. Every other package passed (88 ok); this was the only red.

```
--- FAIL: TestGatewayFixQuitsOnlyAMagpie (0.61s)
    gateway_takeover_test.go:137: another program's port: {OK:false Reason:not-magpie PID:14122 Path:/Users/yetone/Library/Android/sdk/emulator/qemu/darwin-aarch64/qemu-system-aarch64-headless Port:49510 Version:0.1.550 Error:}
```

The test's fake gateway answered on 127.0.0.1:49510, and the take-over correctly said not-magpie. But it named the PID and path of an Android emulator's qemu running on mote. So the lookup from port to process found qemu on 49510, not the test's child process. qemu holds that port number on some address, maybe on the wildcard address or on IPv6, while the fake holds 127.0.0.1. Either way, the lookup matches on the port number alone.

The test itself is fine about what it wants. The gap is real for users too: the take-over can name, and with a magpie match end, a process on another address that shares the port number. It isn't caused by 608c1543e, which doesn't touch internal/gui or internal/proc.

To look at:
- whether `proc.ListeningOn` (or whatever takeOverGateway uses to find the holder) matches the listening address as well as the port;
- a regression test with a second listener on the same port on another address (`[::1]` or `0.0.0.0`).

Related, but a different cause: #3649 is a timeout in this test from the /proc walk.

issue.title: catalog: a dashed-date snapshot id (gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29) has no window or price

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
A relay that lists a model under OpenAI's dated snapshot id (`gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29`, a dashed YYYY-MM-DD date) now gets the base model's reasoning levels in Codex's catalog (the fix for maomao_00001's report on Discord). Its context window and price are still unknown, though: `catalog.SameModel` strips 8- and 6-digit snapshot dates (`-20250514`, `-250514`) but not the dashed form, so ContextOf and the price lookups miss it, and Codex's catalog gets context_window 0 for that id.

Not changed in the levels fix because SameModel is used by groups, prices and families too, and widening it needs its own check of each of those.

Repro: a provider with model `gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29` and the 2026-11-07 models.dev rows; `catalog.ContextOf("gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29")` is 0 while `gpt-6.1-sol` has its window.

issue.title: TestGatewayKeyLimitCLI red on origin/main b39a793c9: 5-hour window's Reset-Start is not exactly 5h

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body: go test -count=2 -run TestGatewayKeyLimitCLI ./internal/cli fails every time on origin/main b39a793c9 (macOS, PST), gateway_keys_cli_test.go:197: Start 21:27:42.270314, Reset 02:27:42.280028 (the two differ by ~10ms), so `st.Reset.Sub(st.Start) != 5*time.Hour`. The test takes Reset-Start as exactly 5h while budget.Of rounds Start and Reset from different clock reads. Found while shipping the Claude tier-alias change; not caused by it.
